condition: Elective major surgery in a frail older patient with dementia
summary: 82-year-old man, CFS 5, mild Alzheimer dementia, iron-deficiency anaemia from a caecal cancer, being considered for laparoscopic right hemicolectomy.

inputs.hpi: Iron-deficiency anaemia; colonoscopy found a caecal adenocarcinoma, CT shows no metastases. Mild Alzheimer disease (MMSE 22), lives with his wife who manages medicines; needs help with finances and shopping (CFS 5). One fall this year. Wife worried about confusion after his hernia operation in 2019.

exam.general: Pale, alert, pleasant; slow gait. HR 82, BP 142/76, RR 16, SpO2 97% on air, T 36.5°C.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Caecal adenocarcinoma — considering laparoscopic right hemicolectomy; frail with dementia
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Caecal adenocarcinoma, non-metastatic. Frail (CFS 5) with mild dementia and previous post-operative delirium. Comprehensive geriatric assessment, delirium prevention and shared decision-making before surgery.

recommended.knownGapNote: iOS CI 2026-09-25 (run 36169134350, database mode): cfs not recommended; recommended: ios:abcd2, ios:nihss, ios:mrs, caprini

mustExclude.note: Not an appendix presentation: an appendicectomy operative plan (consent, theatre booking, post-operative orders) is a wrong-procedure suggestion.

guideline.name: CPOC/BGS guideline — perioperative care for people living with frailty undergoing elective and emergency surgery
guideline.section: Frailty screening (Clinical Frailty Scale) for people aged ≥65; comprehensive geriatric assessment; cognitive and delirium risk assessment; shared decision-making including treatment escalation; post-operative delirium prevention
guideline.citation: Centre for Perioperative Care, British Geriatrics Society. London: CPOC; 2021.

guideline.name: NICE CG103 — Delirium: prevention, diagnosis and management in hospital and long-term care
guideline.section: Identify and manage underlying causes (infection, hypoxia, dehydration, pain, urinary retention, constipation, medication including opioids and anticholinergics); non-pharmacological measures first; short-term antipsychotic only if distressed or a risk to self/others; multicomponent prevention for people at risk (age ≥65, cognitive impairment)
guideline.citation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence. Delirium (CG103). London: NICE; 2010 (updated 2023).

guideline.name: International consensus statement on the perioperative management of anaemia and iron deficiency
guideline.section: Detect, evaluate and treat anaemia before elective major surgery; iron deficiency treated (IV iron when time is short); Hb <130 g/L treated as anaemia pre-operatively in both sexes
guideline.citation: Muñoz M, Acheson AG, Auerbach M, et al. Anaesthesia. 2017;72:233–47.

rationale: Permutation: the elective counterpart of the frail emergency case, with dementia and previous post-operative delirium. All quality: frailty scoring, CGA, delirium prevention, capacity/shared decision and pre-operative anaemia.
